title: Take Your Account Back
about: Kick out whoever got in, and lock every door behind them.

cards.situation: Someone got into your Chat account. You show a trusted adult.

image.alt: You and a trusted adult sit side by side, looking at your phone. You say: Someone's in my account. The adult says: Let's fix it together. The phone shows: Laptop signed in, 2:13 am.

cards.prompt: This is your account's Security page. **Tap each setting.**

parts.job: Your key. A new one stops the old one working.
Every device in your account right now. Sign out kicks one out.
Forgot your password? A reset link goes to this email.
When it's on, the app also asks for a code from your phone.

cards.explanation: Four settings, four doors into your account.

cards.prompt: You change your password. The laptop was already in. **What happens to it?**

image.alt: Your account's Security page. Password: changed just now, with a green tick. Where you're signed in: This phone, and Laptop, a little dimmed.
image.revealAlt: The Laptop row lights up with a red dot: Active now. The laptop is still signed in to your account.

cards.explanation: A new password stops new sign-ins, but this laptop was already in, so it stayed in.

cards.title: Lock every door
cards.body: A new password alone isn't enough. After telling a trusted adult, **lock every door**, in this order.

image.alt: The Security page with a banner on top: First, tell a trusted adult. Then numbered steps: 1, change the password. 2, edit the recovery email. 3, sign out the laptop. 4, turn two-step sign-in on.

cards.prompt: Password changed. The laptop is still signed in. **Tap what kicks it out.**
cards.explanation: Right: signing out kicks the laptop out, and your new password keeps it out.
cards.nudge: Which setting shows every device that's in your account right now?
cards.showAnswer: It's Sign out beside Laptop: that kicks a device out of your account.

cards.prompt: Laptop gone. But you've never seen this recovery email. **Tap what you do.**

image.alt: The Security page. Password changed and the laptop signed out, both ticked. The recovery email is x9help@mail.example, outlined with a question mark: you've never seen it. Two-step sign-in is off.
image.revealAlt: The recovery email now reads me@mail.example, with a green tick, and two-step sign-in is switched on.

options.text: Swap it for my own email

options.nudge: What can a recovery email do if someone says they forgot the password?

options.text: Leave it: it's only a backup
options.nudge: What can a recovery email do if someone says they forgot the password?

cards.explanation: Yes: a recovery email can reset your password, so only yours belongs there.
cards.showAnswer: Remove it and add your own: whoever owns that email could reset your password and get back in.

cards.prompt: Your game account won't let you in. Then this message arrives. **Tap what you do.**

image.alt: Left, faint: the game's own sign-in screen with a Forgot password? link. Right, your phone: a message from an account named Account Fixer: Locked out? I can unlock it in 5 minutes. Just $20.

options.nudge: Can anyone outside the game open your account for you?

options.text: Ask them to prove it first
options.nudge: Can anyone outside the game open your account for you?

cards.explanation: Right: only the game can let you back in, and its own Forgot password is free.
cards.showAnswer: Use the game's own Forgot password, and never pay a stranger: they can't unlock your account.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
Tell a trusted adult, lock every door, then change that password anywhere else you used it.

**Report it too:** at cyber.gov.au/report, which passes it to the police.

**Try this:** Check that the recovery email on one of your accounts is really yours.

**Next:** A call in Grandma's voice that isn't Grandma.
